investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing Due to Swarm Agent Quota Exhaustion (HTTP 409)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) are failing in production with identical HTTP 409 conflict errors indicating the swarm agent quota of 100 has been reached. The AURA observability eval cannot provision a new agent to validate VM readiness or runtime state because the upstream swarm layer is rejecting all new agent creation requests.
investigation.rootCause: The production swarm backend has hit its hard agent quota limit of 100. Every POST /api/agents request is rejected with a 409 conflict response containing the message "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because the AURA eval check depends on successfully creating a new agent to assert vmIdPresent and remoteState, the entire remote-agents feature check tree is blocked at the creation step. No evidence points to a transient network or auth issue; the error is deterministic and quota-specific.
proof: POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 with body: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null}

All three sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) carry the identical 409 error message, confirming the failure is not isolated to one check path but is systemic across the entire remote-agents feature.
The inner swarm error code is 'conflict' with message 'conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', indicating a hard quota ceiling enforced by the swarm layer, not a transient error.
Eval evidence object is empty ({}) for all three checks, confirming no agent was created and no downstream assertions (vmIdPresent, remoteState) could be evaluated.
Latency for all three failing calls is low (1426 ms, 1261 ms, 1129 ms), consistent with an immediate quota-rejection response rather than a timeout or infrastructure hang.
The check ran at 2026-06-14T03:42:20Z in the production environment, ruling out a staging/dev misconfiguration.
possibleCauses: [MOST LIKELY] The production swarm environment has accumulated 100 live agents and the quota ceiling has been reached. This could be caused by AURA eval agents from previous runs not being cleaned up (leaked agents), leaving no room for new provisioning.
[LIKELY] The AURA eval check does not perform teardown of the agent it creates after each run, causing agents to accumulate over time until the quota is exhausted.
[POSSIBLE] A separate workload or tenant in the same swarm namespace/org is consuming agent slots, leaving none available for the observability eval account.
[POSSIBLE] The quota limit of 100 is a per-org or per-environment ceiling that has not been raised to accommodate growth in agent usage, and legitimate production agents have filled the quota.
[LESS LIKELY] A swarm-side bug is incorrectly counting active agents or failing to release slots for terminated agents, causing phantom quota consumption.

reproductionSteps.command: GET /api/agents?limit=100 (or equivalent list endpoint) and count total active agents in the production org to verify the 100-agent ceiling is reached.
reproductionSteps.details: If the response returns 100 agents or the API returns a count equal to the quota, the quota exhaustion is confirmed.

reproductionSteps.details: Filter the agent list for agents created by the AURA observability eval identity (e.g., by name prefix, label, or creator ID). Determine if prior eval runs left agents running without cleanup.

reproductionSteps.label: Inspect swarm quota configuration
reproductionSteps.details: Check the swarm backend configuration or admin panel for the per-org agent quota setting to confirm the limit is 100 and whether it is adjustable.

reproductionSteps.details: Inspect the remote-agent-create check implementation to determine whether it deletes or terminates the agent it creates after each eval run completes.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Blocked by Swarm Agent Quota Exhaustion (HTTP 409)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed simultaneously in production at 2026-06-14T03:42Z with identical HTTP 409 conflict errors. The swarm backend rejected every POST /api/agents request with "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100", meaning the observability eval could not provision a test agent and therefore produced no evidence payload at all.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend has reached its hard agent quota limit of 100 for the target organization or environment. Every attempt to create a new agent via POST /api/agents returns HTTP 409 with the nested error "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because the AURA eval check depends on successfully creating a fresh agent before it can poll state or verify runtime readiness, the quota exhaustion causes a total cascade failure across all three sibling checks. No evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) were populated, confirming the failure occurred at agent creation before any lifecycle state could be observed.
proof: All three checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) returned HTTP 409 with identical error body: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null}
The nested swarm error explicitly states 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', indicating the swarm layer enforces a hard cap of 100 agents.

All three checks have empty evidence objects ({}) — none of the required contract fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) were populated, confirming failure at the creation step before any state polling could occur.
Failure timestamps are tightly clustered (03:42:22Z–03:42:24Z) with low latencies (1129–1426 ms), consistent with fast rejection at the quota-enforcement layer rather than a timeout or network issue.

The outer error message 'swarm agent already exists' alongside 'quota exceeded' suggests the swarm may also be tracking a leaked or un-cleaned agent from a prior eval run that was never deleted, compounding the quota pressure.
possibleCauses: [MOST LIKELY] The swarm environment used by AURA evals has accumulated 100 live agents and hit the hard quota cap — likely due to prior eval runs that created agents but did not successfully delete them (leaked agents), exhausting the available slots.

[LIKELY] The AURA eval teardown/cleanup step for POST /api/agents is failing silently or not being reached on error paths, causing each failed or partial eval run to leave a residual agent behind, gradually consuming quota.

[POSSIBLE] The quota limit of 100 is shared between AURA observability eval agents and real user-provisioned agents in the same environment/org, and organic user growth has consumed the remaining capacity.
[POSSIBLE] A recent deployment or configuration change lowered the quota ceiling or changed the org/environment scoping of the quota, causing previously-sufficient headroom to disappear.
[LESS LIKELY] The swarm backend is misreporting quota exhaustion due to a counter bug (e.g., agents that were deleted are not being decremented from the quota counter).

reproductionSteps.details: If the retry succeeds after freeing a slot, this confirms quota exhaustion as the root cause rather than a swarm counter bug.

investigation.title: Image Generation Stream Fails with SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) — Agent Runtime Harness Unreachable
investigation.summary: The image generation stream eval failed immediately after `generation_start` because the agent runtime returned a 404, emitting a `SESSION_OPEN_FAILED` error frame before any progress or completion frames could be produced. Both required evidence fields (`frameTypes` and `imageUrlPresent`) are absent, confirming the stream never advanced past session initialization.
investigation.rootCause: The agent runtime harness is unreachable at the configured endpoint (LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL). The 404 response during session open indicates either the harness process is not running, the endpoint path has changed due to a version mismatch between the eval harness and the deployed runtime, or the environment configuration points to a stale or incorrect URL. The stream terminates in under 2.1 seconds (latencyMs: 2034) with no image frames, which is consistent with an immediate connection-level rejection rather than a processing failure.
proof: Frame 1 (generation_start) confirms the stream was initiated with mode=image, meaning the eval harness itself started correctly.
Frame 2 (generation_error) carries code=SESSION_OPEN_FAILED and an explicit 404 message: 'agent runtime endpoint not found (404): the harness is unreachable or running an incompatible version.'
Frame 3 is a bare message event with null data and empty raw payload, indicating the stream was closed without any content after the error.
latencyMs of 2034ms is far below the warningLatencyMs threshold of 180000ms, confirming the failure is an immediate rejection, not a timeout.
Required evidence fields frameTypes and imageUrlPresent are both missing from the collected evidence, meaning no generation_completed frame and no artifact URL were ever emitted.
The expectedOutputContract assertion frameTypes contains generation_completed was never satisfied, and imageUrlPresent equals true was never satisfied.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The agent runtime harness process is not running or has crashed in the production environment, causing all session-open requests to return 404.

[Likely] The LOCAL_HARNESS_URL or SWARM_BASE_URL environment variable is misconfigured — pointing to a wrong host, port, or path — so the 404 is returned by a reverse proxy or load balancer that has no matching route.
[Likely] A recent deployment changed the harness API route structure (version mismatch), making the previously valid session-open endpoint path return 404 on the new version.

[Possible] A network policy, firewall rule, or service mesh configuration change in the production environment is blocking or misrouting traffic to the harness endpoint, resulting in a 404 from an intermediary.
[Less likely] The harness container or pod was evicted or scaled to zero in production and has not been rescheduled, making the endpoint transiently unavailable.

investigations.title: Image Generation Stream Fails with SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) — Agent Runtime Harness Unreachable
investigations.summary: The image generation stream eval failed immediately after `generation_start` because the agent runtime returned a 404, emitting a `SESSION_OPEN_FAILED` error frame before any progress or completion frames could be produced. Both required evidence fields (`frameTypes` and `imageUrlPresent`) are absent, confirming the stream never advanced past session initialization.
investigations.rootCause: The agent runtime harness is unreachable at the configured endpoint (LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL). The 404 response during session open indicates either the harness process is not running, the endpoint path has changed due to a version mismatch between the eval harness and the deployed runtime, or the environment configuration points to a stale or incorrect URL. The stream terminates in under 2.1 seconds (latencyMs: 2034) with no image frames, which is consistent with an immediate connection-level rejection rather than a processing failure.
proof: Frame 1 (generation_start) confirms the stream was initiated with mode=image, meaning the eval harness itself started correctly.
Frame 2 (generation_error) carries code=SESSION_OPEN_FAILED and an explicit 404 message: 'agent runtime endpoint not found (404): the harness is unreachable or running an incompatible version.'
Frame 3 is a bare message event with null data and empty raw payload, indicating the stream was closed without any content after the error.
latencyMs of 2034ms is far below the warningLatencyMs threshold of 180000ms, confirming the failure is an immediate rejection, not a timeout.
Required evidence fields frameTypes and imageUrlPresent are both missing from the collected evidence, meaning no generation_completed frame and no artifact URL were ever emitted.
The expectedOutputContract assertion frameTypes contains generation_completed was never satisfied, and imageUrlPresent equals true was never satisfied.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The agent runtime harness process is not running or has crashed in the production environment, causing all session-open requests to return 404.

[Likely] The LOCAL_HARNESS_URL or SWARM_BASE_URL environment variable is misconfigured — pointing to a wrong host, port, or path — so the 404 is returned by a reverse proxy or load balancer that has no matching route.
[Likely] A recent deployment changed the harness API route structure (version mismatch), making the previously valid session-open endpoint path return 404 on the new version.

[Possible] A network policy, firewall rule, or service mesh configuration change in the production environment is blocking or misrouting traffic to the harness endpoint, resulting in a 404 from an intermediary.
[Less likely] The harness container or pod was evicted or scaled to zero in production and has not been rescheduled, making the endpoint transiently unavailable.

reproductionSteps.details: A mismatch here would confirm a version skew root cause.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing Due to Swarm Agent Quota Exhaustion (HTTP 409)
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) are failing in production with identical HTTP 409 conflict errors indicating the swarm agent quota of 100 has been reached. The AURA observability eval cannot provision a new agent to validate VM readiness or runtime state because the upstream swarm layer is rejecting all new agent creation requests.
investigations.rootCause: The production swarm backend has hit its hard agent quota limit of 100. Every POST /api/agents request is rejected with a 409 conflict response containing the message "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because the AURA eval check depends on successfully creating a new agent to assert vmIdPresent and remoteState, the entire remote-agents feature check tree is blocked at the creation step. No evidence points to a transient network or auth issue; the error is deterministic and quota-specific.
proof: POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 with body: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null}

All three sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) carry the identical 409 error message, confirming the failure is not isolated to one check path but is systemic across the entire remote-agents feature.
The inner swarm error code is 'conflict' with message 'conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', indicating a hard quota ceiling enforced by the swarm layer, not a transient error.
Eval evidence object is empty ({}) for all three checks, confirming no agent was created and no downstream assertions (vmIdPresent, remoteState) could be evaluated.
Latency for all three failing calls is low (1426 ms, 1261 ms, 1129 ms), consistent with an immediate quota-rejection response rather than a timeout or infrastructure hang.
The check ran at 2026-06-14T03:42:20Z in the production environment, ruling out a staging/dev misconfiguration.
possibleCauses: [MOST LIKELY] The production swarm environment has accumulated 100 live agents and the quota ceiling has been reached. This could be caused by AURA eval agents from previous runs not being cleaned up (leaked agents), leaving no room for new provisioning.
[LIKELY] The AURA eval check does not perform teardown of the agent it creates after each run, causing agents to accumulate over time until the quota is exhausted.
[POSSIBLE] A separate workload or tenant in the same swarm namespace/org is consuming agent slots, leaving none available for the observability eval account.
[POSSIBLE] The quota limit of 100 is a per-org or per-environment ceiling that has not been raised to accommodate growth in agent usage, and legitimate production agents have filled the quota.
[LESS LIKELY] A swarm-side bug is incorrectly counting active agents or failing to release slots for terminated agents, causing phantom quota consumption.
